THE QUESTION PUT TO ME: does mn_petition_juvenile_as_adult-set's petition state its own statutory ground on its own face? I did not read mn_petition_15218-set and I hold no claim on it; every sentence below is measured on my own family's bytes and on the pinned sources it binds.

ANSWER, PART ONE -- YES, AND THE TICK IS GENUINELY THE WHOLE ELECTION ON THIS FORM. EXP102 item 9 is titled 'Qualification for Expungement. Why do you qualify for an expungement?' and prints eleven ballot boxes: eight on packet page 4 and three on packet page 5. I read all eleven on the delivered page and can give a reason for each. I traced the page-4 content stream with a text-matrix interpreter and the eight box glyphs sit at baselines y 660.00, 572.00, 516.00, 475.20, 403.20, 315.20, 227.20 and 136.80, all at x 90.4, glyph advance 12, cid <0706> mapped to U+2610. The only vector ink this build adds to that page is six path tokens -- '0 0 0 RG / 93.2 573.2 m / 99.66 579.61 l / S' and its mirror -- an X spanning x 93.2-99.66, y 573.2-579.61. The census's own outline for the box at baseline 572.00, taken from the embedded glyf bbox, is x0 92, y0 572, x1 100.86, y1 580.81. The X is inside that outline on both axes and inside no other. So the mark lands on item 9 box 2, which prints 'You were certified or referenced for prosecution as an adult for a crime you committed when you were a juvenile.' That IS this route's statutory ground and it IS on the face of the petition.

WHY A TICK IS ENOUGH HERE, AND WHY ONLY TWO OF ELEVEN BOXES COULD EVER HAVE BEEN THIS FAMILY'S: each item-9 box prints its own bracketed order instruction. Box 1 (controlled substance dismissed and discharged under Minn. Stat. Sec. 152.18) and box 2 (certification or reference for adult prosecution) BOTH print '[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Record - Minn. Stat. Sec. 609A.02, subd. 1 or 2 (court form EXP106).]'. Boxes 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 all print '[... (court form EXP105).]' and box 11 prints '[... (court form EXP107).]'. This family binds EXP106 and binds neither EXP105 nor EXP107, so nine of the eleven boxes are structurally unavailable to it and the census records all ten unelected boxes as NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_THIS_ROUTE. EXP106 packet page 9 finding 1 then carries the matching pair as two mutually exclusive limbs -- 'and was sentenced pursuant to Minn. Sec. 152.18' OR 'following certification or reference to district court for prosecution pursuant to Minn. Stat. Sec. 260B.125' -- and EXP106 is the judge's instrument, correctly filled to its caption only, so neither limb is elected by the build. On this form suite the petition's election point is item 9 and nowhere else: EXP102 prints no other statutory-ground field. Item 6 asks for the authority in prose, and the packet leaves it to the participant, which I address under KNOWN_PREFILLS and REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING below rather than treating as an election defect. So the pair is real, the tick is the election, and the near-clone gate is right not to flag it.

ANSWER, PART TWO -- AND THE PETITION REFUTES ITS OWN TICK TWO PAGES LATER. This is the finding, and it is on my family alone. The delivered petition swears at item 3 (packet page 2) 'List your date of birth: 1991-04-17' and at item 10 (packet page 5) 'Date of offense: 2019-08-04'. That participant was 28 years, 3 months and 18 days old on the date of the offence. The box ticked two pages earlier says the crime was committed 'when you were a juvenile'. A court reading pages 4 and 5 of this petition together reads an election the same document's own sworn facts make impossible. Item 10 also swears 'Type of offense: Fifth-degree possession of a controlled substance' -- which is the subject matter of item 9 box 1, the Sec. 152.18 branch, not of box 2. The boundary fixture is worse: it keeps the same date of birth and the same offence date and extends the charge to 'Fifth-degree possession of a controlled substance, aiding and abetting, continued for dismissal', a continued-for-dismissal disposition, on a petition that elects certification for adult prosecution. Nothing anywhere in this family's collected fact set bears on juvenile status, on age at the offence, or on a Sec. 260B.125 certification; the controlling registry names this track's one disposition as 'adult_conviction_after_certification' and that disposition appears on neither delivered fixture. I read the build script's CANONICAL and BOUNDARY objects and neither contains a certification fact or any age-consistency assertion. So: the whole of the distinction between this remedy and an ordinary petition is one tick and seventeen pages of prose that describe a different remedy. The tick is correct and the paper under it is not.

rows.theEncryptedSourceQuestionAnswered:
ASKED: confirm the source receipt binds the official AES-256 encrypted binary and not one of the review derivatives in data/rcap-all50/overlays/rescued-encrypted-pdfs/. ANSWER: it binds the official binaries, and the West Virginia problem does not recur -- but the receipt states the DERIVATIVE'S byte length beside the OFFICIAL binary's SHA-256, on both documents.

WHAT I DID. I materialised data/rcap-all50/overlays/rescued-encrypted-pdfs/ with git sparse-checkout add -- it was outside my checkout -- and hashed everything in play. The two bound sources verify byte-exact on disk at the paths the receipt names: CIV_EXP_02_A at 'private/source-imports/Nationwide_Recovery_Pool_2026-09-02/LegalEase Delaware/download.aspx.pdf' is f2820f713b9f8e0fb1c0095886e7184d56fda06eef7f65af014ab48922b7839a, 179445 bytes; CIV_EXP_08_A at '.../LegalEase Delaware/source-acquisition-2026-09-04/civ_exp_08_a-sc-new-order-granting-expungement-after-pardon-form.pdf' is 0f7666ac6877b4d482a71c5303ecb199792f713e3c728adb2308b86945505d5b, 1128070 bytes. Both still carry /Encrypt with /StdCF /CFM /AESV3 /Length 32 in their trailers, so both bound identities are the encrypted originals as published. pikepdf opens each with an empty user password and reports 1 page and 44 and 36 AcroForm fields respectively, matching the receipt's formIdentityNote.

THE COMMITTED RESCUED DERIVATIVE IS BOUND NOWHERE, AND IS THE SAME REVISION. data/rcap-all50/overlays/rescued-encrypted-pdfs/delaware-download-aspx-rescued.pdf is bc39abcda95beef0acd46f27b3220fefe26fb4b8eac7989a3ea9f509147c3182, 178625 bytes, unencrypted -- a third byte set, equal to neither the official binary nor this build's transport derivative, and cited by no field of this family's receipt, field map or wiring. I compared it against the official anyway, because the West Virginia lane's finding was a revision mismatch and not a binding mismatch: both are 1 page, both carry 44 AcroForm fields, and their field-name sets are identical with no field on either side that the other lacks. So even the committed rescue is the same revision here. Nothing like WV's 71-against-75 is present.

I REPRODUCED THE TRANSPORT DERIVATIVES BYTE-EXACTLY. Running the receipt's own recipe -- pikepdf.open(pinned_source).save(out, deterministic_id=True) on pikepdf 10.12.0 -- gives 4da3c8988b7c28af8485809b1b62b0b196e6722c11def06248085721b337921c at 178713 bytes for CIV_EXP_02_A and 90218a00a4535bae0bd726583fce67f468dd99c404130857aaeb08b2ff161925 at 1123088 bytes for CIV_EXP_08_A, which are exactly the derivedSha256 and derivedByteLength the receipt declares for each. The pattern is reproducible from the committed record by a reader who did not build it, which is the strongest thing that can be said for it. Neither derivative is committed and neither appears in the delivered packet.

THE DEFECT I DID FIND, and it is in exactly the place the WV warning points at. In documents[0] the receipt pairs sha256 f2820f71... (the official binary) with byteLength 178713 -- which is the DERIVATIVE'S length, not the official's 179445. documents[1] does the same: sha256 0f7666ac... (official) beside byteLength 1123088, the derivative's, against the official's 1128070. Both byteLength values are exactly the derivedByteLength stated a few fields below them. The binding itself is sound because this factory binds by content digest and both digests are right, so I have not scored SOURCE_IDENTITY a FAIL for it -- the packet is built on the right documents. But the receipt as committed describes each bound identity with another document's size, and a checker verifying the binding by length rather than by hash would read a mismatch on both official forms of this family. It should be corrected by the lane that owns the builder.
rows.theSbiCoverLetterQuestion: The builder's account is accurate and I can add where the phrase comes from. No committed record used by this build names an SBI cover letter: the packet-set manifest declares component de_pardon_expungement-cover-sheet-3 with role cover_sheet, outputStrategy custom_pleading, requirement required, order 3, and no content specification; the track registry's packetSet block carries the same three components and no more. The phrase lives one record further back, in data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/DE.memo.json, which declares this track's cover_sheet component with notes 'SBI cover letter.' and states the sibling § 4374 track's filing rule as 'Assemble the packet in the prescribed order: petition, proposed order, SBI cover letter, then the certified criminal history dated within 45 days.' That memo gives the instrument a name and nothing else -- no addressee, no content, no form number. What is delivered on packet page 3 is a FILING COVER SHEET headed 'IN THE SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE', which names the route and its statute, identifies the petitioner by name, date of birth, address, telephone and criminal case number, lists the filing's three documents in order, and names the certified criminal history as attached by the petitioner. It is addressed to the Court, not to the State Bureau of Identification, it carries no signature block, states no fee, deadline, clerk practice or service rule, and asserts nothing about eligibility -- I read the whole page on both fixtures. If an SBI cover letter is a distinct instrument addressed to the Bureau with required content, then the builder is right that it is not built, and no committed record in this repository says what it would have to contain. That is a question for whoever owns DE.memo.json and for counsel; it is not something I can settle by measurement, and I have not scored it as a missing component because the two records the brief told me to score COMPONENT_SET against declare a cover_sheet and a cover sheet is delivered.
rows.theIsoDateQuestion: The builder's factual account holds on the bytes and the decision is sound as far as measurement reaches. I read both official forms through their proven-equivalent derivatives: CIV_EXP_02_A prints 'Date of Birth' and CIV_EXP_08_A prints 'Date of Birth', and neither prints (mm/dd/yyyy) or any other order beside, beneath or inside the blank -- there is no printed line from which an order could be read. The delivered bytes carry '1978-03-14' on the canonical fixture and '1955-12-02' on the boundary, on the petition, on the proposed order and on the cover sheet alike, so the three pages agree with each other. ISO 8601 is unambiguous, is not contradicted by anything either form prints, and cannot be misread as a different date -- unlike, say, 03/14/1978 against 14/03/1978. Writing mm/dd/yyyy would require inferring a convention from the jurisdiction rather than from the paper, which is the inference the finalizer exists to refuse, and the refusal is consistent: this build also declined to guess the county from the mailing address. WHAT I CANNOT DECIDE: whether the Prothonotary of the Delaware Superior Court will accept an ISO date on these two forms is a clerk-practice question, and no committed record in this repository states a Delaware date convention -- I grepped the track registry, the packet-set manifest and the DE intake memo and none carries one. Fabricating a clerk's practice is out of bounds for this lane. So: sound as built, correctly raised by the builder in its approval request, and it needs a person who knows the Prothonotary's practice. It is not a defect I can prove and I have not scored it as one.

The assertion box is not. Box lines, the three signature and jurat blanks, the two court-assigned case numbers, and the order's paragraph 5 and judicial date and signature.
